items.title: Traditional Joinery in Steel… But Did I Make It Too Light?
items.description: In this video I’m building a 3.6m wide steel gate using rivets and traditional joinery, with very little welding. It’s lighter than I originally planned, so I wasn't sure how it would handle flex. The build uses a mix of mortice and tenon joints in steel along with riveted connections, rather than relying on welding for everything. As always I'm happy to answer any questions. items.title: Making a Chisel Unlike Anything You’ve Seen
items.description: In this video I’m making a fully custom chisel using mosaic Damascus steel, ivory micarta and a fluted handle with silver wire inlay. It’s not meant for everyday woodworking — this project is all about learning new techniques and trying to make something special. The Damascus was made by my mate Jackson Rumble (Mastersmith knife maker) and I’ve been saving it for a few years. If you enjoy toolmaking, Damascus steel, metalwork, or detailed woodworking builds, you’ll like this one. As always I'm happy to answer any questions. items.title: How to Make the Easiest Patterned Veneers - Turn Regular Plywood into Designer Plywood
items.description: I’ve made a fair amount of patterned wood before — some of it pretty complicated — but this time I wanted to try something quicker and more approachable. In this video, I’m turning plywood scraps into thin pattern veneers and using them to upgrade regular plywood. It’s pretty fast, surprisingly effective, and a great way to make a cool looking panel for furniture projects. As always I'm happy to answer any questions. items.title: Making Unique Dividers – Just Hand Tools and Patience
items.description: Limited Time Plans Bundle: https://paskmakes.com/premier-top-tier-woodworking-plans-bundle In this video, I’m making a pair of dividers entirely by hand using only basic tools the only power tool I use is a drill. It was an awesome challenge which I really enjoyed. I’ve wanted to make a pair of these for a few years, and after seeing a pair made by Seth Gould during a recent scissor-making course with my mate Matt, I finally decided to give it a go. The design is more difficult than it needed to be but I really liked the unique wing so I went with it. If you're interested in getting hold of some quality hand tools like many of the ones I use in this video, check out my good friend Corin's website and support a small scale workshop https://www.niroc.com.au As always I'm happy to answer any questions.
